_doc: The unspent ceiling per research domain — read minus ruled-on, as of the day it was written. Generated by tools/measure_research_spend.py --rebaseline. RAISING A NUMBER HERE IS A DECISION: it says the project chose to read further ahead of its adjudication, and the PR that raises it says why. Lowering one is free and is what spending a domain does.

raised.why: T-0571 (PR #714) read Fergus's 1843 Chicago directory — 2,695 entries — into dev while this branch was open. The read is legitimate and already merged; this branch inherits it and cannot spend it. The ceiling is raised to admit it, NOT to excuse it: T-0588 (rank 2) spends the directory on the businesses layer and T-0587 already spent 67 of it onto resident cards, so this domain has live spend tickets and the number should come back down.

T-0578 read volume 2 (C-H): 1,987 kept cards, plus the 40-card precision draw this ratchet also counts as read. It did NOT read ahead of its ruling — T-0590's gate does not allow that any more, and it is the reason this raise is 1,622 and not 2,027. The same PR extended tools/rule_newberry_leads.py from volume 1 to every volume read and ruled the 227 new leads volume 2 offers under T-0590's own ladder: 546 leads on 947 cards, 146 candidates testable in a held work, 400 refused, 0 merges, 0 discriminators found. So the SPEND went up with the read, from 542 cards to 947, and what remains unspent is what has always been unspent here — the cards standing under no lead at all, a surname nobody in this town carries. Two measurement faults this exposed are on T-0596 and neither is an excuse: the precision sample's 80 rows count as read though they are re-readings of records already counted, and count_spent sees only rulings carrying an id anchor, so crosswalk.json's one pass and five written refusals count as zero.

lowered.why: T-0590 ruled on all 319 leads volume 1 offered, anchored to the 542 distinct cards they stand on: 240 refused, 79 candidates in a work this project already holds, 0 merges. Lowering a ceiling is free and is exactly what spending a domain does. The remaining 2,077 are volume 1's cards that stand under no lead at all - a surname nobody in this town carries - and they come down when a later ticket rules the surnames out in bulk or the volumes 2-4 tickets replace the arithmetic.
